analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read occurs because getMessageLength() unconditionally reads handshakeLayer->length2 (2 bytes) from m_Data after casting to ssl_tls_handshake_layer, without first ensuring m_DataLen >= sizeof(ssl_tls_handshake_layer). For truncated handshake fragments (<4 bytes), this dereference reads past the buffer end. Crash is observed from SSLHandshakeLayer constructor calling message->getMessageLength() on a message created from insufficient remaining bytes.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: FuzzTarget feeds a malformed PCAP packet that is parsed as TCP->SSL. In SSLLayer::parseNextLayer/createSSLMessage, SSLHandshakeLayer is instantiated for a record marked as handshake. Inside SSLHandshakeLayer loop, createHandshakeMessage() may return a message object for the current cursor, and then getMessageLength() is called. If remaining handshake bytes at curPos are shorter than ssl_tls_handshake_layer but still reach this call path, getMessageLength() performs a 2-byte read of length2 out of bounds, triggering ASan heap-buffer-overflow.
